Seminar Title:

Numerical study of viscoelastic fluid flow past an elliptical cylinder in a laminar flow regime

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Chemical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Nicky Pattnaik ( Rollno : 522ch1005)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

New Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

10 Sep 2026 16.30 Hrs

Contact:

Akhilesh Kumar Sahu

Abstract:

There is a class of industrially important materials, including rubbers, polymers, and their derivatives, that exhibit a combination of viscous fluid-like and elastic solid-like characteristics, resulting in viscoelastic behaviour. Even the addition of a small amount of polymer to a Newtonian solvent such as water can introduce significant elastic effects into the resulting fluid. Understanding the flow behaviour of such complex fluids is important in applications involving polymers, food processing, biological systems, slurries, suspensions, emulsions, and pastes.

While considerable research has been conducted on Newtonian and non-Newtonian flows past circular and other cylindrical bodies, comparatively limited attention has been given to viscoelastic flow around elliptical cylinders with different aspect ratios. In this work, numerical simulations are performed to study the flow of a viscoelastic fluid past an elliptic cylinder. The governing equations are solved using RheoTool, an open-source toolbox based on OpenFOAM, employing the finite volume method. The computational domain and mesh are generated using the BlockMesh and SnappyHexMesh dictionary of OpenFOAM. The effects of the elliptic cylinder aspect ratio, Reynolds number, Deborah number, and solvent viscosity ratio on the flow characteristics are considered.

Three aspect ratios, E = 0.5, 2.0, and 5.0, are considered for Re =10 and 100, with Deborah numbers of De = 0.5 and 2.0, and solvent viscosity ratios of &beta = 0.5 and 0.85 in an unconfined channel. The flow behaviour is characterised using the drag coefficient, streamline patterns, wake structure, and vortex shedding in the vicinity of the elliptic cylinder. The results show that increasing the Deborah number enhances the influence of fluid elasticity, while changes in the solvent viscosity ratio modify the relative contributions of the solvent and polymeric components. The aspect ratio also has a significant influence on the wake characteristics and hydrodynamic forces. These results provide insight into the combined effects of cylinder geometry and fluid elasticity on viscoelastic flow past elliptic cylinders.

The findings aim to enhance the current understanding of viscoelastic fluid behaviour around elliptical cylinders, providing valuable insights for industrial applications involving complex fluid dynamics.
